_README: kubegym service-model config. Every physical constant carries its own `calibrated` flag,
`source` string and `required_for_claims` flag. The top-level `calibrated` is the AND over
every field marked `required_for_claims`; it is what every result row stamps. A single
uncalibrated required field makes the whole run non-reportable. That is deliberate.
PORTED VERBATIM from the source testbed's cluster_config.json (schema cluster-config-2).
Every field below that also existed there keeps its value and its `source` string
byte-for-byte; see `_port` for the provenance of the port itself.
calibration_note: UNCALIBRATED OVERALL. Cold start, KV budget and the decode step-time model on batch<=8 are MEASURED on the GPU testbed (vLLM 0.25.1 / Qwen3-1.7B / single L40S 46GB). The per-class OUTPUT-LENGTH DISTRIBUTION is still a labelled placeholder from length_model.py, prefill throughput was never measured, and decode step time above batch 8 is an unmeasured affine extrapolation. No number produced by this simulator may be reported as an empirical result.

chunked_prefill.source: NOT MODELLED. vLLM v1 enables chunked prefill by default; the simulator charges a whole-prompt prefill that stalls the replica's decode. This overstates the TBT spike caused by an admission and understates the TTFT of a long prompt under load.

class_predictor_accuracy.source: Sensitivity knob, not a measurement. 1.0 = the controller reads thinking_mode as-is. Below 1.0 the class signal handed to belief-based controllers is corrupted with that per-request probability of being correct, standing in for a real prompt-length predictor's error.

class_signal.source: The router genuinely observes `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking` on every request, so conditioning a belief on thinking mode uses no privileged information. CAVEAT, see controllers_report.md 6.2: in the emitted traces thinking_flip_prob=0.0, so thinking_mode is a NOISELESS proxy for the length class. Set class_predictor_accuracy < 1.0 to inject predictor error.

control_interval_s.source: Matches the Kubernetes HPA default sync period (--horizontal-pod-autoscaler-sync-period, default 15 s) so that the HPA baseline runs at its real cadence. All controllers are given the same decision cadence.

decode_batch_extrapolation_above_8.source: PLACEHOLDER / UNVERIFIED. Throughput was measured only at batch 1, 4 and 8. Above batch 8 the simulator extrapolates the affine step-time model, which predicts near-linear aggregate throughput (e.g. 872 tok/s at batch 16, 1591 tok/s at batch 32). Real engines saturate; the affine extrapolation is therefore OPTIMISTIC about large batches and biases the simulator toward under-provisioning being cheap. Must be measured at batch 16/32/64 before any claim.

decode_step_time_s.source: LEAST-SQUARES FIT to measured single-replica decode throughput from vLLM's own iteration logger: 60.3 / 232.6 / 460.2 tok/s at 1 / 4 / 8 concurrent requests. Model t_step(b) = a0 + a1*b seconds per scheduler step, where one step emits one token for each of the b running sequences. Max relative error on the three fitted points: 1.05%.

gpu_cost_per_replica_hour_usd.source: NORMALISED UNIT, not a price quote. Cost is reported primarily as replica-seconds (GPU-seconds); the USD column is replica-hours x 1.0 so it is a pure rescaling. Substitute a real instance price only when quoting money.

kv_tokens_per_replica.source: MEASURED on the GPU testbed: KV budget per replica at --gpu-memory-utilization 0.21, vLLM 0.25.1, Qwen3-1.7B.

max_num_seqs.source: PLACEHOLDER: vLLM's documented default max_num_seqs. Not read off the live server config. In practice KV pressure binds before this does at these sequence lengths.

metric_scrape_interval_s.source: Design choice matching the control interval. On the real testbed this is the Prometheus scrape interval and introduces staleness the simulator currently models as zero.

n_replicas_max.source: GPU testbed track: 4 co-resident vLLM replicas on one L40S 46GB, each --gpu-memory-utilization 0.21, --max-model-len 8192.
n_replicas_max.note: Hard ceiling of the physical testbed. The simulator will refuse a target above this unless --allow-hypothetical-replicas is passed, which stamps hypothetical:true.

n_replicas_min.source: Design choice: at least one replica must serve.

output_length_distribution.source: Delegated to length_model.py, which returns calibrated:false and the labelled placeholder lognormals until measured_lengths.json lands. THIS IS THE DOMINANT UNCALIBRATED INPUT: it sets the offered token load.

preemption_policy.source: Models vLLM's recompute-style preemption: a preempted sequence returns to the head of the waiting queue and re-pays prefill on its already-generated prefix. Output tokens are not lost (deterministic-decode assumption). vLLM's exact victim-selection order was NOT read from source; the simulator preempts the most-recently-admitted sequence.

prefill_tokens_per_s.source: PLACEHOLDER, NOT MEASURED. Prompt-prefill throughput was never measured on the testbed. Governs TTFT and the decode stall a new admission causes. Any TTFT number from this simulator is placeholder-derived.

replica_cold_start_s.source: MEASURED, n=9: median 31.90 s to serving-ready, IQR [31.82, 32.40]. This is the actuation lag d.

replica_teardown_s.source: MEASURED but n=2 only (0.54 s for 1 replica, 1.31 s for 4 concurrent). TREAT AS AN UPPER BOUND / weak evidence.

router_policy.source: PLACEHOLDER for the real router's balancing policy: dispatch to the READY replica with the fewest running+waiting requests. The real router's policy must be recorded and matched here before any claim.

slo.source: DESIGN CHOICE pending calibration, not a measurement. tbt_p95_s = 0.05 s (20 tok/s per stream) sits above the measured single-stream 58 tok/s, so it is reachable; ttft targets are provisional and must be set from the measured single-replica capacity curve.
slo.note: These targets define the cost-SLO objective every controller is tuned against, so they must be identical across controllers (tune.py enforces this).

replica_bringup.source: VERIFIED OPERATIONAL CONSTRAINT on the GPU testbed: starting several vLLM engines concurrently fails KV sizing, so replicas were brought up ONE AT A TIME. The pool therefore serialises boots: the i-th replica requested at t becomes ready at max(t, last_pending_ready) + replica_cold_start_s. This is a lifecycle policy, not a measured scalar; `calibrated: true` records that the sequential path is the one that was actually exercised, not that a timing was fitted.
replica_bringup.note: The source simulator booted replicas in PARALLEL (every replica requested at t ready at t + cold_start), which makes multi-replica scale-up look faster than the verified path, i.e. OPTIMISTIC. Set to 'parallel' to reproduce the source simulator exactly; the parity harness does. The two policies are identical whenever scale-up adds one replica at a time, which is the common case for every controller in the suite.
